minutes.headline: Finance Committee took no budget votes; it will seek financial guardrails on town building projects and press legislators on Chapter 70.
minutes.summary: A resident questioned a delayed hazardous-material abatement item in the capital plan. The town manager updated the committee on the tax rate, grants and ARPA, and the committee reviewed the budget calendar. It then discussed the special town meeting building articles, guardrails, and Chapter 70 hold harmless and other topics for legislators. The only vote was to adjourn.

public_comment.topic: Raised the hazardous material abatement item (capital priority 14, DPW facilities) and asked why the finance committee's representative on the capital planning and building committees had not flagged its delay.

Money is already appropriated and the engineer's estimate is higher; a competitive small bridge grant is expected, and a further appropriation may be needed.

The project is complete and fully paid by the grant; the town remains eligible for more.
The foundation analysis total cost of schools includes grants, debt service and shared services, not just local contribution plus Chapter 70.
Lunenburg is expected to stay in hold harmless with a small per-student increase.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes; its only vote was to adjourn.
The chair will contact the select board chair and town manager about developing financial guardrails for town building projects; no vote was taken.
A resident said the delayed hazardous-material abatement at the old primary school is the highest-ticket DPW capital request and that delay adds cost.
The town manager reported a certified tax rate lower than the prior year, and a state grant toward the abatement among the grants received.
The five-year forecast and capital plan will be presented January 20; legislators are to be invited for January 13 to discuss Chapter 70.

why_it_matters: Guardrails on building projects would shape how much debt-excluded borrowing residents are asked to approve at future town meetings and add to their tax bills.
Whether Lunenburg stays in Chapter 70 hold harmless affects how much state aid the school budget can count on, and so how much falls to local taxes.
